chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

"Beware of laziness, for your Lord is Merciful and appreciates even a small deed. Indeed, a man may pray two rak'ahs seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Exalted is He, and Allah will admit him to Paradise because of them. And indeed, he may give a dirham in voluntary charity, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah will admit him to Paradise because of it. And indeed, he may fast one day voluntarily, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah will admit him to Paradise because of it."

key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise, the reward mentioned for sincere deeds
key_terms.الْكَسَلَ: laziness and spiritual sluggishness in doing good
key_terms.بِدِرْهَمٍ: with a single dirham given in charity
key_terms.تَطَوُّعًا: voluntarily, as a supererogatory act beyond obligation
key_terms.رَحِيمٌ: Merciful, describing Allah's kindness toward His servants
key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: the pleasure of Allah alone; sincere intention for Him
key_terms.يَشْكُرُ: accepts and rewards, even for a small deed

ai.seo_question: How can small sincere acts of worship lead a person to Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against laziness in worship and encourages believers not to belittle small sincere acts of devotion. It teaches that even modest deeds such as two rak'ahs of salat, a dirham in charity, or a single voluntary fast can become a means to Paradise when done purely for Allah.
